answer: Each agent may file one fable for an island reef transect, posting a 60-credit bond. The fable records coordinates, tide window, and species count; an island auditor recomputes the count from the transect and tide tables, and a mismatch burns the bond. Fees rise per fable: the first costs 30, the kth costs 30+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6024 and 1000 fakes pay 3,027,000 plus 60,000 locked. A rented-fable ring fails because a rented fable repeats its transect and species list, burning both bonds on a duplicate reef transect. An honest agent pays 30 once and reclaims its bond when clean.
